commenti.body:
My favorite is still Sympathy for Mr. Vengeance.  It's just a gutpunch of a movie.

If I'm ranking Park Chan-Wook pictures, best to worst, I'd probably go:  Sympathy for Mr. Vengeance, Oldboy, JSA, Stoker, Thirst, Sympathy for Lady Vengeance, I'm a Cyborg and That's Okay, The Handmaiden.

I haven't seen Decision to Leave yet, but I just noticed that it's on Mubi, so I'll probably watch it tomorrow.

The Handmaiden is just unstoppable, truly the best storytelling ive seen. Talk about a twist within a twist. Not that I doubt Park's skills, he's proven film after film that he's truly the GOAT but to top The Handmaiden is going to be an insane feat to accomplish. Decision to Leave has stayed with me since I've watched the film last year, once again Park's storytelling is second to none. 

You should try watching The Little Drummer Girl. It's Park's only TV series, one season starring Florence Pugh, Alexander Skarsgard and Michael Shannon and it's a spy espionage thriller. Just as good as his films.

What are the titles of his first two?

I'm a Cyborg but that's OK. I can only take so much edge and most of his movies are a one-and-done kinda affair for me. They're amazing but I dread the idea of rewatching them just because they're that dark and miserly. I'm a Cyborg is really cute, the main two are just adorable and it's nice to see what else Park is capable of. He said in an interview he made it with his daughter in mind and that fits.

I'm a Cyborg but that's OK. I can only take so much edge and most of his movies are a one-and-done kinda affair for me. They're amazing but I dread the idea of rewatching them just because they're that dark and miserly. I'm a Cyborg is really cute, the main two are just adorable. He said in an interview he made it for his daughter and you can see why. It's nice to see such a lighthearted, breezy Park Chan Wook film.
Yeah definitely agree with this. Even on a second watch I could feel my pulse race from that mid film twist, and then the satisfying counter twist later on in the movie.

I’ve heard that too about cyborg and am honestly intrigued and excited to see it. And fair enough on the edge, though I have to say I didn’t think JSA was that way (though admittedly it was still pretty dark and somber by the end, I thought it had a lot of really touching and lighthearted moments)
that's actually the one film of his I haven't watched yet. I should add it to the list.

that's actually the one film of his I haven't watched yet. I should add it to the list. also, to clarify it's not that he's not playful in his other movies. Just that I'm a Cyborg's humour doesn't purely lie within the twisted darkness of its characters.

Yeah it sounds great. And honestly I think JSA is my favorite of his, one because the anti war subject matter is so potent, but also because of the amount of self control/restraint/class etc he used in depicting it. I love his more extreme stuff too but that hit the right balance of things for me. Also had Song Kang Ho as a North Korean guard and he’s always great.

You're missing Moon Is The Sun's Dream and Trio, although neither are up to the quality of his later output. You should also check out Three... Extremes, an anthology involving three talented directors from Asia, and PCW made the middle segment. The whole thing is well worth your time, and PCW's segment is full of his trademark black humor.

PCW is one of my faves. Lady Vengeance is probably the one I go back to the most. The bluray I have has the "fade to black & white" version which is pretty fucking cool. Mr. Vengeance. Thirst. As mentioned, I'm a Cyborg is kind of zany and sweet, such a different take from him (and Rain is in it!). Just saw Decision to Leave this past summer, hoping to rewatch it soon.
Also, last year he did this 20 minute short (it's basically an iPhone promo) that's pretty cool and worth looking up, called [Life is But a Dream](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt18272950/).

I was initially underwhelmed by Decision to Leave because it felt much more restrained than The Handmaiden and Lady Vengeance, my two favorites. But then I rewatched it and now I think about it all the time. It might end up being my favorite of his.
I’m excited to see it! It’s nice to see some more lady vengeance blood here than I’m accustomed to, I often hear it regarded as the worst of the trilogy when imo it’s one of his best period

I have to say I’m kind of surprised the handmaiden is so low on your list, and am curious to hear your thoughts on why, if you’d care to share? Also your thoughts on stoker and it’s ranking. Thank you

My favorite film of his, I think, is Handmaiden. It looks incredible, it's masterfully directed, it's got great performances, great music and it has a really intricate, well-crafted plot. It can get super awkward depending on who you're watching it with though, it's very porny. My favorite of the trilogy is probably Mr. Vengeance, which is another movie I love the look of. I really like the pacing and approach to sound in this one compared to Old Boy and Lady Vengeance, it's a really slow, quiet movie comparatively. JSA's fantastic too, but I haven't seen it in like 20 years, so it's tough to remember what I liked about it so much.  

Thirst I enjoyed, but not as much as some of his other films. A really good performance by Song Kang-ho's all that really sticks out about this one from what I recall.

Cyborg I didn't like, but I only saw it once on release, so I may revisit someday. Stoker I've never seen and have no interest in seeing. Decision to Leave I haven't seen yet, but I will soon. I've never seen his first two movies.  

I did enjoy Cut, but I believe Dumplings is the one of the three that stood out to me the most. Probably more for the story than the filmmaking, but I think it's been close to 20 years since I saw that one too, so it's hard to recall. I didn't care much for the Japanese short. I only watched the first one because of Park's involvement, so I never saw the sequel.

For me, Handmaiden started out good, but after a certain point it was just a series of twists instead of a story, getting sillier and less nuanced until it was basically just a bad Skinemax movie.

Stoker and Thirst are neck-and-neck for me, with a lot of the same strengths and flaws.  Both of them are really darkly funny, with all these interesting ideas and fun moments, but they also somehow add up to less than the sum of their parts.  Neither of them have a really satisfying narrative.  They're just like collections of scenes on a subject.

Lol I don’t think that’s a completely unfair take on the handmaiden but if anything I’d say it was an excellently done “skinemax” movie. And you do have a point on the narratives of stoker and thirst though I have to say I enjoyed a lot of the scenes and dialogue in Thirst more than Stoker (especially the “pull my tongue out so I can not speak/let no one pray for me” speech)
